llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed website monitor with optional Vercel and GA4 delegation; its sensitive behavior is purpose-aligned and user-controlled.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads OpenClaw state/config and selected Vercel/GA4 credential values for enabled delegated commands; this is clearly disclosed and limited to passing them to the corresponding subprocess.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The base skill requires Node only; optional Vercel/GA4 features require separately installed skills, including a branch-pinned Vercel dependency for log support.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions route user questions to explicit CLI commands and include safety guidance such as not inventing URLs or asking users to paste tokens.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It writes bounded state/log files and can create OpenClaw cron jobs only with schedule --apply; the systemd timer is a manual fallback documented in examples.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently implement uptime checks, scheduled alerts, and optional Vercel/GA4 reporting for website monitoring.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install for uptime monitoring if you are comfortable with local state files and scheduled jobs. Before enabling Vercel or GA4, review the delegated skills too, use least-privilege credentials where possible, and keep includeMessages off unless you accept that application log text may contain sensitive data.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Credential pass-through for Vercel and GA4 is real, but SKILL.md frontmatter and prose disclose the exact variables and openclaw.json keys, and the values are passed to the matching delegated skill rather than printed or written by Web Observer.
[AE1] expected: The referenced delegated skills are runtime dependencies that may not be present in this package; this is not evidence of evasion, but users should review those optional skills before enabling Vercel or GA4 modules.
[RA1] unexpected: The cited service file line is a comment telling users to edit the SKILL_DIR path in a copied systemd unit; it is not self-modifying code.
[PE3] expected: The credential-related code reads configured OpenClaw skill entries and environment variables, not arbitrary credential stores; this is proportionate to scheduled delegated API polling.
[RA2] expected: Persistence exists as state files, cron jobs, and an optional systemd timer, all disclosed and tied directly to monitoring and alert deduplication.
[SDI-4] expected: The docs distinguish side-effect-free check from scheduled watch/vercel-watch/digest commands that update alert state; the inspected code matches that distinction.
[SQP-2] expected: Vercel token setup is documented through OpenClaw configuration; additional file-permission and token-rotation guidance would be useful, but the behavior is not hidden.
[LP3] expected: Network, filesystem, environment, and subprocess use are significant but narrowly described: uptime contacts configured URLs, state lives under OpenClaw state, and subprocesses are spawned without a shell.
